scenes.title: Where and when
narration: Dabus has been sustained in Perak for roughly 300 years.
Tradition holds that it originated in the era of the Islamic prophet Muhammad as a pastime and soldiering practice designed to instil bravery, train combatants, and summon spiritual strength.

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: Conducted under the spiritual authority of a Khalifah, the dance represents warrior valour, religious invocation, dexterity, and collective heroism.
Today it is a living tradition.

scenes.title: Listen
narration: Performances feature singers who chant religious songs of praise.
Musical accompaniment is provided by the rebana, a traditional frame drum.

The sonic signature is defined by the steady resonance of rebana frame drums accompanying vocal chanting. Singers recite religious verses of praise, providing an earnest, elevated spiritual atmosphere to guide the heroic movements of the troupe.

scenes.title: The people
narration: Key historic teachers include master Muhammad Abil Hassan al-Rifai, his students Ahmad Mahyuddin and Fakir Muhammad of India, and Nakhoda Lembang of Batu Bara, Aceh.
In Perak, traditions spread across Pasir Panjang Laut, Sitiawan, Lumut, and Teluk Intan.
Lineage traces pedagogically through Sufi teacher Muhammad Abil Hassan al-Rifai to disciples Ahmad Mahyuddin and Fakir Muhammad, transmitting through maritime networks linking Aceh and coastal Perak.
